did_you_know.text: In biblical language, the “heart” is not only the seat of emotion but also of thought and will. Thus, “a heart to know” means true understanding.
The word “shekhar” means an intoxicating drink, not necessarily wine. The Bible often distinguishes between wine and other intoxicating beverages.
Heshbon was an important city east of the Jordan, usually identified with Tell Hesban in modern Jordan. Bashan was a fertile region east and northeast of the Jordan.
The word “taskilu” is related to the Hebrew word “sechel,” meaning understanding. Here it means not only to learn, but to act wisely and succeed.
The phrase “from your woodcutters to your water drawers” includes every level of society, from leaders to people doing basic labor. It emphasizes that everyone shares in the covenant.

The covenant is presented as a relationship that does not belong only to those present at the ceremony. It also includes future generations, showing that one generation’s actions affect those who follow.

In the ancient world, idols and ritual objects were made from materials such as wood, stone, silver, and gold. Naming these materials highlights the physical nature of idols, unlike belief in a God who is not a statue.
“Poison and wormwood” are images of bitter, even poisonous plants. The expression therefore describes a person or idea that can spread bitterness and harm to others.
Sodom and Gomorrah are traditionally associated with the Dead Sea region, but their exact locations remain debated. Sulfur and salt create a vivid image of a ruined land unable to produce crops.
